# CC review of FineMath math evaluation and candidate screening

CC reviewed through subscription-safe `claude -p` with `env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, Opus 5 at maximum effort. The OAuth subscription account was verified. Read-only access was restricted to the repository; shell, edits and delegation were disabled. The original review and bounded follow-up are preserved in cc_review.md and cc_followup.md.

The initial review missed a runtime error: native PALOMA and the new math examples used different attention-mask tree structures. The first evaluation failed before accepting results. The repair supplies one all-zero segment per math example; a native mixed-batch regression test verifies unchanged causal attention and correct separate weighted means, including final padding. CC's follow-up checked the repair. The retry evaluates exactly the same eight checkpoints and scored token populations.

Implemented the useful review suggestions: preserve unverified diagnostics before the PALOMA check; pin the dataset, loader and attention-mask source; identify the zero-fraction control by unique name; validate unscored BOS and specify boundary-token handling; collect complete and partial results with observed minima, boundary flags, runner-up and neighboring gaps. The actual GSM8K object schema had already been verified before launch; its original solution markup is intentionally retained.

Two candidate claims required correction. The archived synthetic math/code/thinking curves include worse 28.971-epoch points after their 14.486-epoch minima, so those minima are interior observed points. The regional Nemotron Math Textbooks Parquet schema contains plain text, verified with a 57,336-byte footer read. CC accepted both corrections and withdrew its unsupported prediction that FineMath-4+ would minimize near p30.

Both reviews agree that no archived domain establishes >10 optimal epochs on common Uncheatable. The corrected shortlist for discussion is Nemotron Math Textbooks and Stack-Edu Python, with Proof-Pile2 arXiv as backup. Dataset descriptions motivate hypotheses; they do not predict the ordering of optima in the current tiny-model setting. Existing Wikipedia and FineMath curves remain part of the screening record.

Wait for FineMath's math likelihood curve. If it already provides the desired high-epoch response, consider scoring existing Wikipedia proxies on the same math evaluation before training another math domain. This extra evaluation and any new candidate training require the next user decision. New training is proxy-only; targets remain deferred.
title: Math evaluation retry and CC candidate review
